audit.whatIsWrong: diffRating and carryRating were empty strings although breakdown.difficulty and report[14] both read 6/10 and 6/10.
audit.why: Blank rating fields render an empty badge and contradict the prose already on the page. Enum fields, exempt from the length band.

audit.whatIsWrong: The why-lines contradicted their own side tokens on four of seven rows: whys[2], whys[3] and whys[4] all say 'Warwick-favoured' while win[2]/win[3] say 'Skill' and win[4] says 'Dr. Mundo'; whys[5] says 'Skill' while win[5] says 'Dr. Mundo'.
audit.why: The side tokens agree across both layers (full phases[] and content win[] are identical), and that shape — Warwick early, Dr. Mundo from 6 — is what a 52.05% Dr. Mundo win rate over 1120 games supports. So the tokens are right and the why-text is stale. The packet's own levelChart is explicitly flagged defective for this matchup, so it is not the arbiter here.
audit.corrected: whys[2], whys[3], whys[4] and whys[5] rewritten to state the side their tokens already carry, with a real mechanical reason each. No side token touched, so no atomic chart group is needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Primal Howl (E) appears nowhere on the page, and Jaws of the Beast was described only as 'heals him for a chunk of the damage dealt'.
audit.why: Two decisive interactions were absent. (1) Jaws of the Beast deals damage based on your MAXIMUM health — Dr. Mundo's entire build is maximum health, so every Heartsteel and Warmog's stack makes his Q hit harder and heal him more, and armour does not reduce that scaling at all. (2) Primal Howl gives him 2.5s of damage reduction and then fears everyone nearby for 1s on expiry or recast — that is exactly the window in which your Heart Zapper burst is meant to cash, and the fear walks you out of your own W radius.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text now states the max-health scaling; spikes[2].text, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t now carry Primal Howl's 2.5s damage reduction and 1s fear.

audit.whatIsWrong: Infinite Duress was listed as a flat 90s in breakdown.cooldowns, report[5] and implicitly report[9].
audit.why: Riot data has it at 110/90/70. At rank 1 that is a 110-second window, twenty seconds longer than the page claims — the difference between a safe step-up and a suppress. Primal Howl's 15/14/13/12/11 was not listed at all.
audit.corrected: 110s at rank 1 / 70s maxed, plus Primal Howl at 15s rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[11] Common Mistakes did not name the biggest execution error in this lane.
audit.why: Warwick's passive heals him for his bonus magic damage below 50% health and TRIPLES that healing below 25%. Dr. Mundo's Q deals damage based on the target's CURRENT health, so it hits softest exactly when Warwick is lowest. Chipping him to 20% and expecting the kill is how this lane is thrown.
The packet flagged 'Land Infinite Duress' in wants.foe[2] as a probable wrong ability name. It is a false positive — Infinite Duress is Warwick's real R name in the kit file. No edit made.

edits.after: Skill: his max-HP Q bite trades even with your full Level 3 kit.

edits.after: Warwick's Jaws of the Beast (Q) deals damage off your MAXIMUM health and heals him for it, so every HP item you buy feeds him and armour answers none of it. Blood Hunt (W) then runs you down below half.

edits.before: The lane evens out around first item: his Q sustain still trades well, but your regen and bulk start matching his healing — a skill window where positioning and E timing decide trades.
edits.after: The lane turns at first item: Primal Howl (E) gives him 2.5s of damage reduction and then fears you for 1s, so hold your W burst until that window closes — after it, your regen wins the rest.

edits.before: - Warwick Infinite Duress (90s): matchup-defining — His all-in lock. Dodge it. Track it before every commit. - Your ultimate: spend it on kill windows, never on waves. - Summoners: track his Flash after any close call — it changes every dive call.
edits.after: - Warwick Infinite Duress (110s at rank 1, 70s maxed): a 1.5s suppress — never stand alone in its path. - Primal Howl (15s at rank 1): 2.5s damage reduction, then a 1s fear. - Your ultimate: kill windows only. - Track his Flash after a close call.

edits.before: Track Warwick’s Infinite Duress (90s): His all-in lock. Dodge it. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Infinite Duress is 110s at rank 1, not 90 — and Primal Howl fears you 1s after 2.5s of damage reduction.

edits.before: Extend into his heal. Get caught by his R. Fight at low HP early. Chip damage doesn’t get to borrow the ultimate.
edits.after: Chipping him to 20% and expecting a kill — below 25% his passive healing triples, and your Q scales off current health.

notes: Two facts were missing from the entire page and both change how the lane is played: Jaws of the Beast scales off Dr. Mundo's MAXIMUM health (his own build feeds it, and armour is irrelevant to it), and Primal Howl exists at all — 2.5s damage reduction into a 1s fear on a 15s cooldown, which is precisely the window Heart Zapper wants to cash in. Infinite Duress was also mis-stated as flat 90s when it is 110s at rank 1.
